messages:
eva: Heads-up — nightly eval for rwd-3b-quant4 shows a sharp regression on long-context prompt set, 46/200 failures, many look like dropped instructions or truncated continuations.
ml-nightly-bot: nightly-eval: rwd-3b-quant4 | failures=46 | regressions=+22 | report: https://ci/internal/nightly/2204100000 | attached sample ids: 84, 127, 190
anya: can you paste an example failure (prompt + output)? trying to see whether this is tokenizer truncation vs KV loss.
eva: sample 127 below — prompt is a multi-step instruction with reference context (>> indicates system context):
```
>> System: You are a helpful translator. Keep code blocks intact.
User: Translate the following instructions into French and preserve numbered steps:
1) Open the config file at /etc/service/conf.toml
2) Replace the value of throttle_ms to 150
3) Restart the service with `systemctl restart svc`
```
Model output (bad):
"1) Ouvrez le fichier de configuration.
2) Redémarrez le service."
— missing step 2 detail and the code snippet.
raj: interesting — that looks like the instruction got dropped mid-context, not a simple truncation (we'd see the tail cut). Could be KV eviction at a boundary losing earlier keys. Any pattern with token index?
tom: I ran the repro locally with the same model binary + quant artifact. Command used:
```
python -m rwd_eval.runner --model rwd-3b-quant4 --prompts long_prompts/127.jsonl --seed 42 --max-tokens 4096
```
Output matches EVA's example. When I reduce `--max-tokens` to 1024 the generation is fine.
anya: that suggests the runtime is mishandling long sessions/KV windows rather than tokenizer cut. What's the model variant? same checkpoint but quantized artifact from q4a pipeline?
eva: yes exact same checkpoint, artifact tag `q4a-2026-03-10`. We also saw regressions start after yesterday's runtime deploy (deploy-220409-nightly) per infra-bot below.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: promoted rwd-runtime v1.18.3 to prod (220409T23:10) — includes KV eviction refactor and async prefetch change.
sahil: ping @raj @anya — can one of you toggle `KV_DEBUG=1` on a repro run to dump KV slot/seq meta? I want to see if entries are being evicted incorrectly when sequence numbers wrap.
anya: will run with KV_DEBUG and a small patch to print {slot,seqnum,token_idx} at prefetch/evict hooks. putting up a reproducer run now.
anya: quick log snippet from KV_DEBUG run:
```
[KV] slot=64012 seq=65535 -> append idx=16384
[KV] slot=64012 seq=65536 -> evict slot=64012 (age=1) reason=wrap_bound
[KV] append failed: mapping missing for seq=65536
```
anya: looks like we hit a seqnum wrap (16-bit overflow) and eviction logic used the old bound, causing a hole. That would drop earlier context references.
raj: that matches a bug I suspected in the refactor: we switched seqnum arithmetic to unsigned 16-bit for perf and didn't handle wrap in the eviction comparator. I'm bisecting the runtime commits now.
eva: is this specific to the quant artifact or CPU? we've only seen it on quant4 so far (hosted infra runs quant variants for longctx sets).
tom: I ran the same long prompt on the unquantized cpu binary and it passes. So far failure surface only on GPU/quant path in prod.
anya: possible explanation — the quant runtime path uses a different session id mapping and hit higher seqnum values quicker, exposing the 16-bit wrap. If so, unquantized path didn't exercise it.
sahil: next steps: (1) raj to identify offending commit and open rollback or patch, (2) anya to collect full KV dumps for failed ids and upload to GH-1234, (3) tom to run nightly eval with a patched runtime locally to confirm. I'll create a ticket and flag oncall.
raj: opened GH-1234 with reproducer + suspected commit 7c9b2f3, marking P0.
eva: thanks. if someone can push a temporary mitigation (treat seqnum as 64-bit or add wrap guard) that's safest until we patch properly. Also notify Dedicated customers if SLA might be affected.
anya: I'll try the 64-bit guard in a debug build and run the nightly repro. ETA ~2h.
ml-nightly-bot: update: nightly rerun queued with debug build by @anya — results expected in ~90m.
tom: noted — will standby to run the quant regression sweep after your build.
sahil: good catch everyone, this explains the lost-instruction symptoms. keep the thread updated, and drop any additional failing sample ids here. :thumbsup:
